title: Nineteen Years of Crowning
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：champion　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 champion 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 my mother was sent to crown ① champion she could not beat, and she said the crowning was the whole of the lesson. The ② champion, meaning the winner and not the title, was nineteen years old and was crowned by whoever came last; champion, she said, is the only thing in a season that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ champion in that season had the same walk, and the ④ champion at the end, meaning the one the crowd kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever crowned properly. Champion, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ champion was the whole of the sport, meaning the defence it carried and not the winner. The ⑥ champion, meaning the defence and not any of that, is the only thing in a sport that everybody fights for and nobody questions; champion, he said, is either something you crown or the only word that means both a winner and a defence. She said the defence is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ champion had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the walk. The ⑧ champion of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nineteen years and eleven years of crowning; champion, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ champion I remember is the one at the end, which was crowned in 1971 and is still described as the youngest in the county. A ⑩ champion, my grandmother said in 1976, is the only thing that improves by being crowned; every champion, she said, is a defence that has agreed to look like a winner. She said the defence was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 冠军（指那位获胜者本身，与那个头衔相对）
C. 固定搭配：crown a champion 为冠军加冕
D. n. 冠军（指那个赛季每一位）
E. n. 冠军（指末尾那一位）
F. n. 卫冕（抽象：它承载的那份守擂）
G. n. 那份守擂（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The champion, meaning the winner and not the title
champion was the whole of the sport
the champion had become a number in a report
The champion of the whole thing
A champion, my grandmother said in 1976

answers.why: crown a champion 意为“为冠军加冕”，1951 年母亲被派去为她赢不了的那位冠军加冕。
champion 意为“冠军、优胜者”，指那位获胜者本身而不是那个头衔，十九岁，由最后来的人加冕。
champion 指那个赛季每一位冠军，每一位都是同样的走路姿势。
champion 指末尾那一位（观众留下的那一位），是唯一有人认真加冕过的。
champion 意为“卫冕”，抽象指它承载的那份守擂，父亲说 champion 就是那项运动的全部。
champion 为抽象用法，指那份守擂本身，是一项运动里人人都争、却没人质疑的东西。
champion 意为“冠军、优胜者”，到 1966 年这位 champion 成了报告里的一个数字。
champion 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是十九岁与十一年的加冕。
champion 意为“冠军”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1971 年加冕，至今仍被说成全县最年轻的。
champion 为抽象总称，祖母说一位冠军是唯一会因为被认真加冕而变好的东西。
